factions.name: Free Peoples Alliance
factions.ideology: Freedom, preservation, and resistance against the domination of Sauron
factions.description: A coalition of all free races in the Arda galaxy united against the Forces of Darkness. Includes Gondor, Rohan, Rivendell, Lothlórien, the Shire, Moria, and the Istari. Bound by ancient alliances and the shared threat of Sauron's return.

military_branches.name: Gondor Host
military_branches.description: The main military force of Gondor, including the Rangers of the North and South

military_branches.name: Rohan Éored
military_branches.description: The cavalry forces of Rohan, masters of fast transit and shock tactics

military_branches.name: Elven Host
military_branches.description: The forces of Rivendell and Lothlórien, led by Elrond and Galadriel

military_branches.name: Dwarven Companies
military_branches.description: The warriors of Moria and Erebor, masters of close combat and mining warfare

military_branches.name: The Istari
military_branches.description: The five wizard-advisors, Maiar bound in mortal form

key_leaders.name: Aragorn II (Strider)
key_leaders.role: Heir of Isildur; King of Gondor and Arnor

key_leaders.name: Gandalf the White
key_leaders.role: Chief of the Istari; guide and strategist

key_leaders.name: Elrond Half-elven
key_leaders.role: Lord of Rivendell; bearer of Vilya

key_leaders.name: Galadriel
key_leaders.role: Lady of Lothlórien; bearer of Nenya

key_leaders.name: King Théoden
key_leaders.role: King of Rohan; ally of Gondor

key_leaders.name: Éowyn
key_leaders.role: Shield-maiden of Rohan; slayer of the Witch-king

key_leaders.name: Faramir
key_leaders.role: Captain of the Rangers of Ithilien; heir to the Stewardship

key_leaders.name: Treebeard
key_leaders.role: Oldest Ent; leader of the Entmoot

strengths: Unity of diverse races and cultures
Ancient knowledge and wisdom from the Elves
The Three Elven Rings provide protection and preservation
Gandalf's strategic genius and Maiar power
Rohan's fast cavalry and Gondor's disciplined infantry
Mithril armor and elven weapons of unmatched quality
weaknesses: Internal divisions and slow to unite
Declining elven power — the age of Elves is ending
Gondor's weakened state after centuries of decline
Saruman's betrayal from within the White Council
The One Ring's corrupting influence on allies
Numerical inferiority against Mordor's endless armies
allies: The Faithful of Harad and Rhûn
enemies: Harad and Rhûn (when allied with Mordor)

factions.name: Mordor
factions.ideology: Domination, order through fear, and the restoration of Sauron's absolute power
factions.description: The dark volcanic empire of Sauron, the central evil power in the Arda galaxy. A scorched system dominated by a red star, where orcs are mass-produced and war machines are forged. The Eye of Sauron watches all.

military_branches.name: Orc Host
military_branches.description: The primary infantry of Mordor, mass-produced in the mines and forges

military_branches.name: The Nazgûl
military_branches.description: Nine wraith-commanders bound to the One Ring, captains of Sauron's air forces

military_branches.name: Troll Forces
military_branches.description: Giant trolls and drakes, used as siege weapons and shock troops

military_branches.name: The Eye's Surveillance
military_branches.description: Sauron's all-seeing intelligence network, using Palantíri and spies

key_leaders.name: Sauron
key_leaders.role: Dark Lord; bearer of the One Ring

key_leaders.name: The Witch-king of Angmar
key_leaders.role: Captain of the Nazgûl; most powerful of the Nine

key_leaders.name: Shelob
key_leaders.role: Great spider of Cirith Ungol; guardian of the passes

key_leaders.name: Gothmog
key_leaders.role: Lord of the Orcs of Mordor

strengths: Overwhelming numerical superiority
The One Ring amplifies Sauron's power
The Eye sees all — superior intelligence and surveillance
Industrial war machine — endless production of troops and weapons
Fortified defenses — the Black Gates and Barad-dûr
Allies in Harad and Rhûn provide additional forces
weaknesses: Dependent on the One Ring — its destruction ends Sauron's power
Orcs are disorganized and prone to infighting
The Palantíri can be used against Sauron by skilled users
Barad-dûr falls when the Ring is destroyed
Cannot operate effectively without Sauron's direct command
The fires of Orodruin are both strength and vulnerability

factions.name: Isengard
factions.ideology: Power through industry and technology; initially independence, later servitude to Sauron
factions.description: A world stripped of nature, converted into a massive factory complex. Saruman the White, once chief of the Istari, corrupted by the desire for the Ring, now produces war machines and Uruk-hai. Initially independent, later allied with Sauron.

military_branches.name: Uruk-hai Army
military_branches.description: Saruman's improved orc-line, larger and stronger than Mordor's orcs, capable of enduring sunlight

military_branches.name: War Machine Division
military_branches.description: Siege engines and mechanical weapons produced in Isengard's factories

military_branches.name: Hunthic Forces
military_branches.description: Men of the Dunland region, led by Gríma Wormtongue's influence

key_leaders.name: Saruman the White
key_leaders.role: Former chief of the Istari; fallen wizard; ruler of Isengard

key_leaders.name: Gríma Wormtongue
key_leaders.role: Saruman's agent; corrupted Théoden for years

key_leaders.name: Uglúk
key_leaders.role: Uruk-hai captain; led the force that captured Merry and Pippin

strengths: Advanced technology and industrial production
Uruk-hai are superior to standard orcs
Orthanc is indestructible
The Palantír of Orthanc provides intelligence
Strategic location between Rohan and Mordor
War machines and siege engines
weaknesses: Saruman's hubris and underestimation of Gandalf
Environmental destruction weakened the realm
The Ents — ancient guardians who can destroy the factories
Dependent on Saruman's leadership
The Palantír was used by Sauron to corrupt Saruman
Helm's Deep proved harder to capture than expected

factions.name: The Nazgûl (Ringwraiths)
factions.ideology: Total servitude to Sauron; domination through fear and terror
factions.description: Nine human kings who were given Rings of Power by Sauron and slowly transformed into wraiths — invisible servants of the Dark Lord. They command the air forces of Mordor and inspire terror across the galaxy.

military_branches.name: Fell Riders
military_branches.description: The Nazgûl on Fell Beasts, capable of space and atmospheric flight

military_branches.name: Wraith Host
military_branches.description: The invisible servants and thralls of the Nazgûl

key_leaders.name: The Witch-king of Angmar
key_leaders.role: Captain of the Nazgûl; most powerful of the Nine

key_leaders.name: The Witch-lords
key_leaders.role: The other eight Nazgûl, lesser but still terrifying

strengths: Invisibility — can move undetected
Terror — their presence inspires paralyzing fear
The Morgul-blade — can turn the wounded into wraiths
Fell Beasts — powerful flying mounts
Bound to Sauron's will — cannot betray him
Immune to most conventional weapons
weaknesses: Vulnerable to elven weapons and water
The prophecy: 'Not by the hand of man shall he fall'
Dependent on the One Ring — its destruction frees them
Sunlight weakens them (though they can still operate)
Can be resisted by those with strong will (Aragorn, Faramir)
Éowyn and Merry killed the Witch-king
enemies: Rohan (the Witch-king founded Angmar to destroy it)

factions.name: Harad
factions.ideology: Southern independence; some factions serve Sauron, others remain neutral or allied with Gondor
factions.description: Hot, tropical star systems with unique flora and fauna. Home to the Haradrim, diverse cultures that range from Sauron's allies to Gondor's trade partners. Known for Mûmakil (war elephants) and exotic warfare.

military_branches.name: Haradrim Host
military_branches.description: The southern armies, including cavalry and Mûmakil

military_branches.name: Corsairs of Umbar
military_branches.description: Pirate fleets from the southern ports, naval threat to Gondor

key_leaders.name: The Haradrim Kings
key_leaders.role: Various chieftains and kings of the South

key_leaders.name: The Captain of the Corsairs
key_leaders.role: Leader of the Umbar pirate fleet

strengths: Mûmakil — massive war beasts that can crush fortifications
Naval power — the Corsairs threaten Gondor's ports
Exotic resources and trade goods
Diverse cultures and fighting styles
Strategic location — control of southern trade routes
weaknesses: Internal divisions — not all Haradrim serve Sauron
The Faithful of Harad remain loyal to Gondor
Less organized than Mordor's forces
Vulnerable to elven and Númenórean tactics
The White Hand cult divides the realm

factions.name: Rhûn
factions.ideology: Eastern nomadic freedom; some factions serve Sauron, others remain independent
factions.description: Vast, open star systems on the eastern rim of the galaxy. Home to the Easterlings, nomadic and warlike peoples. Some are drawn into Sauron's service through the Palantíri, while others (the Útúlië) ally with Gondor.

military_branches.name: Easterling Host
military_branches.description: The eastern armies, nomadic cavalry and infantry

military_branches.name: Útúlië Alliance
military_branches.description: The faction that allied with Gondor against Sauron

key_leaders.name: The Easterling Chieftains
key_leaders.role: Various leaders of the eastern tribes

key_leaders.name: The Lords of Lamedon
key_leaders.role: Gondor's eastern allies

strengths: Vast numbers — the eastern tribes are numerous
Cavalry tactics — skilled riders and pilots
Strategic location — gateway between Mordor and the eastern rim
The Útúlië provide loyal allies to Gondor
weaknesses: Internal divisions — the Útúlië oppose Sauron's faction
Manipulated by Sauron through the Palantíri
Less organized than Mordor's forces
Nomadic lifestyle makes sustained campaigns difficult

factions.name: The Ents
factions.ideology: Protection of the forests and nature; slow to anger but devastating when roused
factions.description: Ancient, tree-like beings — the oldest living beings in Middle-earth. Shepherds of the trees, they are neutral in most conflicts but will act decisively when nature is threatened. Their attack on Isengard was one of the turning points of the War of the Ring.

military_branches.name: Entmoot Host
military_branches.description: The Ents in battle formation — slow but unstoppable

key_leaders.name: Treebeard
key_leaders.role: Oldest Ent; leader of the Entmoot

key_leaders.name: Fastred
key_leaders.role: Second oldest Ent

key_leaders.name: Fimbrethil
key_leaders.role: Treebeard's beloved; an Ent (rare female)

strengths: Immense strength — can uproot trees and destroy fortifications
Extreme longevity — ancient wisdom and patience
Connection to nature — can command the Huorns
Nearly indestructible — conventional weapons are ineffective
Surprise — enemies do not expect trees to fight back
weaknesses: Extremely slow to decide on action
Few in number — their population is declining
The Entwives are lost — a source of great sorrow
Fire is their greatest weakness
Once their purpose is fulfilled, they wander and fade

factions.name: The Blue Wizards
factions.ideology: Independent operation in the East and South; little is known of their activities
factions.description: Alatar (the Brown) and Pallando (the Blue) — two of the five Istari who chose to operate in the East and South, beyond the reach of Sauron's Eye. Their fate is unknown; some say they founded cults, others that they worked secretly against Sauron.

military_branches.name: Eastern Agents
military_branches.description: The Blue Wizards' network of agents and allies in the East and South

key_leaders.name: Alatar (the Blue)
key_leaders.role: Operates in the East (Rhûn)

key_leaders.name: Pallando (the Blue)
key_leaders.role: Operates in the South (Harad)

strengths: Maiar power — though restricted by mortal form
Operating beyond Sauron's direct surveillance
Knowledge of eastern and southern cultures
Independence from the politics of the West
weaknesses: Little is known — their effectiveness is uncertain
May have founded cults that became problematic
Isolated from the other Istari
Cannot directly reveal their power
